ink-quiet.displayName: Ink Quiet (secondary text on tinted fills)

display.purpose: One per entry screen: the page title. Also the sidebar wordmark at -0.02em.

headline.purpose: Company legal name, dashboard page title, the number inside the score ring.

title.purpose: Every dashboard card heading. 16px for the SWOT card only.

body.purpose: Chat messages, country summaries, detail-panel prose.

detail.purpose: The workhorse: SWOT bullets, business bullets, source rows, meta lines, error text.

label.purpose: The system's only uppercase: section labels in the country drawer, tier label above a country name.

micro.purpose: AI disclaimers and table column headers.

shadows.name: seat
shadows.purpose: Every dashboard card at rest. Seats the card on the ground rather than lifting it; the 1px seam border does the separating.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Hover response on clickable cards, paired with translateY(-2px).

shadows.name: lift-profile
shadows.purpose: The profile card's navy-tinted hover lift.

shadows.name: popover
shadows.purpose: The profile context menu — the only floating element that is neither drawer nor modal.

shadows.name: drawer
shadows.purpose: Directional shadow cast leftward by right-anchored drawers (chat, country detail).

shadows.name: modal
shadows.purpose: The deepest layer: centered dialogs (full map, delete confirmation).

shadows.name: accent-glow
shadows.purpose: The system's only colored shadow, under primary green buttons.

shadows.name: scrim
shadows.purpose: Overlay backdrop behind drawers and the delete dialog; 0.55 behind the full map.

motion.name: screen-enter
motion.purpose: Screen entry on form, confirm, profiles and dashboard.

motion.name: overlay-enter
motion.purpose: Same curve at overlay speed, so modals and drawers feel attached to the click.

motion.name: spin
motion.purpose: The 64px analysis spinner and its 18px inline twin in the country drawer.

motion.name: card-lift
motion.purpose: Hover on any clickable card, paired with the lift shadow.

motion.name: map-hover
motion.purpose: Country path hover drops to 0.78 opacity.

narrative.overview:
MarketCompass looks like a briefing a consultant prepared overnight and left on your desk: structured, scannable, confident, and — critically — always the same shape. Two different companies produce two documents you can lay side by side, because the sections, the ranking, the score scale and the SWOT never rearrange themselves to suit the data. The interface's job is to make an AI-generated analysis feel prepared rather than improvised.

That ambition sets the density. This is not a spacious marketing surface and not a dense analyst console. Cards sit on a near-white ground separated by hairline seams, headings are heavy (800) and small, body text runs 12.5–13px, and nothing carries a gradient, a glow or an illustration. The one saturated color in the system is Compass Green, and it earns its loudness by being rare: it marks what is confirmed, what is best, and what you can act on. Everything else is graphite and paper.

The system is deliberately unshowy because the product's whole claim is verification. A screen that looks generated undermines a product whose differentiator is that its inputs are not. Three worlds are rejected outright: the generic AI-product landing (purple-to-blue gradients, glassmorphism, floating orbs, sparkle icons), playful consumer SaaS (mascots, pastel blobs, emoji-led empty states), and the crypto/fintech dark dashboard (dark ground, neon accents, animated tickers). Any of the three would cost the product the credibility it spends its whole pipeline earning.
keyCharacteristics: Near-white ground, white cards, hairline seams — paper, not chrome
One saturated accent (Compass Green) doing signal duty, never decoration
Heavy small headings (800 weight at 15–26px) against light 12.5–13px body
A three-step traffic-light tier system that colors the ranking, the map and the score ring identically
Structural elevation: page → card → popover → drawer → modal, each with its own shadow step
Zero illustration, zero gradient, zero rounded-blob geometry

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Compass Green is the only saturated color permitted for interface intent. If a screen needs a second "look here", the answer is weight, size or position — never a second accent hue. Audit test: on any screen, green should be traceable to action, confirmed fact, or rank 1–5. If it is on anything else, remove it.

rules.name: The Navy-Is-Identity Rule
rules.body: #13294F appears in the logo and wordmark and nowhere else. A navy button, navy heading, or navy border is a defect.

rules.name: The Tier-Means-Rank Rule
rules.body: Green / amber / red never encode sentiment, health or freshness. They encode position in the fifteen — 1–5, 6–10, 11–15 — and every surface showing that scale resolves it through the same tierOf(rank) helper in derive.ts. Never hand-assign a tier color.

rules.name: The Heavy-and-Small Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is carried by weight before size. A heading never drops below 700, and 800 is the default for anything that titles a region. Reaching for a larger size to signal importance is the wrong lever; reach for weight, then for position.

rules.name: The Half-Point Rule
rules.body: This system genuinely uses half-point sizes (11.5, 12.5, 13.5, 14.5, 15.5) and they are load-bearing — 12.5 and 13 are distinct roles, not rounding noise. Preserve them. All type is specified in px, not rem, and no size is fluid; there is no clamp() anywhere.

rules.name: The One-Uppercase Rule
rules.body: Uppercase is reserved for the 11.5px section labels inside detail panels. Buttons, headings, chips and nav are always sentence case.

rules.name: The One-Breakpoint Rule
rules.body: The system currently adapts at 900px only, and the 264px sidebar does not collapse below it. This is the honest state, not a target — any work touching small screens is extending the system, not conforming to it, and should say so.

rules.name: The Ellipsize-Never-Scroll Rule
rules.body: Ranking rows, country names and summaries truncate with text-overflow: ellipsis on a single line. The page body never scrolls horizontally; a too-narrow column shortens its content instead.

rules.name: The Altitude-Is-Meaning Rule
rules.body: Never pick a shadow for looks. Pick the step that matches the layer: a card gets Seat, a hovering card gets Lift, a floating menu gets Popover, an edge-anchored panel gets Drawer, a centered dialog gets Modal. A new shadow value is a new layer, and there are no new layers.

rules.name: The Colored-Shadow Exception
rules.body: Exactly one colored shadow exists — the green glow under primary buttons. Do not tint any other shadow.

rules.name: The Short-Motion Rule
rules.body: Nothing animates longer than 0.4s and nothing animates that the user did not cause. There is no scroll-triggered motion, no parallax, and no decorative loop. The typing dots and the spinner are the only continuous animations, and both report machine state.

rules.name: The Fill-Or-Ink Rule
rules.body: Every semantic color exists in two weights, and the question is never which looks better — it is what the eye is doing. Reading it as a shape? Use the fill. Reading it as letters? Use the ink. A thin graphic (the score ring's arc, a 1px rule) counts as letters. Audit test: if a colored value sits under a fontSize, it must be an ink.

dos: Do put new surfaces on ground (#FAFBFC) with white cards and 1px seam (#EDEFF2) borders. That pair is the settled system.

Do resolve every tier color through tierOf(rank) in derive.ts so the ranking, map, legend and score ring can never disagree — and take `ink` or `fill` from it deliberately, never whichever one is already in scope.
Do reach for weight before size when something needs to feel more important — 800 at 15px outranks 400 at 20px in this system.
Do keep the 16px card / 10px control radius pairing. A new radius value needs a reason that a listed step cannot serve.
Do match the shadow to the layer (Seat / Lift / Popover / Drawer / Modal), not to the mood.
Do preserve the half-point type sizes; 12.5px and 13px are distinct roles.
Do carry the AI disclaimer at 11px Ink Faint under any surface presenting generated analysis, as the SWOT card and country drawer already do.
Do state absence explicitly — #D1D5DB for unranked countries, an em dash for a missing KRS, a dashed-border panel for no saved profiles. Missing data is a designed state.
Do keep #9CA3AF off anything with a fontSize. It is a disabled-state and decoration value now.
donts: Don't use #FAF8F4 or #E8E2D8 in new work. They are legacy warm values pending migration.
Don't introduce a second saturated accent. If green is already spoken for on the screen, the answer is weight, size or position.
Don't use Meridian Navy (#13294F) for anything but the logo and wordmark.
Don't add another near-duplicate green. #16803C has been consolidated onto #15803D; the greens are now #16A34A (region), #15803D (ink) and #166534 (hover), and that is the whole set.
Don't generalize Analyst Violet (#7C3AED). It exists to keep the fourth SWOT quadrant distinguishable and has no other license.
Don't use tier green/amber/red to mean anything except rank position 1–5 / 6–10 / 11–15. Sentiment, health and recency need a different device.
Don't add gradients, glassmorphism, blur backdrops, glow effects, sparkle or orb decoration, illustrated mascots, or pastel blob geometry. Each belongs to one of the three rejected worlds.
Don't animate anything the user did not cause, and don't exceed 0.4s.
Don't let the map be the only path to a country's data — the ranking list beside it carries that duty and must keep carrying it.

Don't reintroduce dead .mc-* rules. .mc-icon-btn, .mc-menu-item, .mc-new-profile-tile, .mc-dropdown-row, .mc-bubble, .mc-top3-card and the mc-pop keyframe are defined in globals.css but referenced by nothing.
